sentences.text: Proceedings have arisen from filing of DAR in FIR No.443/2017 of PS Jyoti Nagar, registered u/s 279/337/338 IPC, in respect of an accident dated 31.10.2017 wherein petitioner Satender suffered grievous injuries.
As per the facts, on 31.10.2017 at about 6.00 a.m. petitioner/injured sat in an auto rickshaw from Chajjupur for going to Loni and in the said auto rickshaw three persons were already sitting.
Petitioner initially refused to sit in the auto rickshaw but on the insistence of auto MACT No.27/2018 Page 1 driver, petitioner sat beside the driver.

It is stated that auto rickshaw was driven in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and when it was about to reach Durga Puri Chowk, driver of the auto rickshaw suddenly turned it due to which petitioner fell down and wheel of the auto run over the leg of the petitioner and he sustained injuries.
Someone called the police and petitioner was removed to GTB Hospital.
Petitioner/injured stated that the auto driver ran away from the spot.

2. In response to the DAR, owner and driver filed the reply/written statement wherein it is stated that respondent no.1 has been falsely implicated in this case by the police in collusion with Dar - Satender vs Rais on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70538189/
1 petitioner.
It is stated that on 31.10.2017 at about 6.15 a.m. no accident took place from the alleged vehicle by respondent no.1 as alleged in the FIR.
It is stated that vehicle was having valid RC and insurance papers.

It is denied that accident took place due to rash and reckless driving of respondent no.1.
3.
Reply/written statement has also been filed by respondent no.3/ insurance company, wherein insurance company took all the plea in terms of Section 134 (c), 147, 149, 157 and 170 of Motor Vehicle Act.

An objection has been taken that as per FIR petitioner could not note down the registration number of offending vehicle and present case is a hit and run case wherein some unknown vehicle caused the accident.
Further objection taken is that petitioner was traveling in the offending vehicle on the front seat in contravention of seating capacity of vehicle.

Further objection has been taken that permit to TSR in Delhi is issued to registered owner who himself is holding a valid TSR driving licence and public service badge and he is not allowed to entrust the same to some other person.

It is stated that only MACT No.27/2018 Page 2 registered owner/permit holder can drive the vehicle and if he entrust the vehicle to some other person, he contravenes the terms and conditions of insurance policy.
However it is stated that vehicle no.DL-1RU-5911 was insured with respondent no.3 vide policy no.0157555699 from 30.09.2017 to 29.09.2018 in the name of Sunil Kumar.

4. On the basis as come on the record, on 19.02.2018 following issues were framed by Ld.
Predecessor of this court:

(1)Whether injured Satender sustained injury during the accident caused by the respondent no.1 by rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle no.DL1RU5911 on 31.10.2017 at 6.00 pm at Durga Puri Chowk, Delhi?
(2)Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

(3)Relief.
5.
In order to substantiate his case petitioner examined three witnesses.
PW1 Satendra Kumar is petitioner/injured himself.
PW2 is Rakesh Saxena stated to be an eye witness.
PW3 is Dr.Deepankar Verma from GTB Hospital who proved disability certificate of the petitioner.
6. Respondent no.1 and 2 have examined witness R1W1 Sudesh Ranjan from Burari Transport Department.
Respondent no.3 examined two witnesses.

R3W1 is Devender Kumar, Record Keeper from Transport Department, Burari, Delhi who proved permit record of offending vehicle and R3W2 is Ms.P Kirthy, Senior Manager of M/s Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited.

sentences.text: 7. I have heard the arguments advanced by Sh.Suman Kumar Roy, learned counsel for the petitioner as well as Sh.Indrajeet & Sh.Ved Tripathi, ld. counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company.

My issue wise findings are as under :
MACT No.27/2018 Page 3  ISSUE No.1 Dar - Satender vs Rais on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70538189/
2 8.
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others.

sentences.text: In order to prove the manner in which accident has taken place, injured Satendra Kumar (PW1) in his affidavit of examination in chief has testified that on 31.10.2017 at about 6.00 a.m. he had to go from Chhajupur and was waiting for an auto at Chhajupur Chowk.
In the meantime a shared auto bearing registration no.DL-1RU-5911 came near to PW1 and he was offered to be boarded in the said auto rickshaw by its driver.
PW1 boarded in the said auto and its driver started driving rashly and negligently.

PW1 further says that offending vehicle was being driven by its driver rashly and negligently at high speed, suddenly took a sharp turn before reaching Durga Puri Chowk, resultantly PW1 fell down on the road from the auto and his leg MACT No.27/2018 Page 4 was run over by the wheel of auto and he sustained grievous injuries on his left leg and other parts of body.
PW2 further says that thereafter he was shifted to GTB Hospital by the help of public where his MLC no.A-3377/30/17 dated 31.10.2017 was prepared.

10. PW1 has been duly cross examined, however nothing has come in the cross-cross-examination with regard to facts stated by PW1 on the aspect of alleged rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
Though he denied that he was sleeping in auto.
Rather PW1 specifically stated that at the time of accident he was in auto bearing no.DL-1RU-5911 which he boarded at Chajjupur.
11. Testimony of petitioner/injured (PW1) has been corroborated by evidence of PW2 Rakesh Saxena who deposed that he is eye witness of the accident.
PW2 deposed that on 31.10.2017 he boarded an auto at Maujpur as he had to go to Shahdara Subzi Mandi.
After running 500 meters at Chajjupur, one passenger i.e. petitioner gave signal to stop the auto and after that he boarded in the same auto.

PW2 says that after running few meters, at about 6-6.15 a.m. at Chajjupur driver of the said auto took a sharp right turn, resultantly passenger sitting beside the driver fell down on the road and injured was run over by the said auto.
PW2 says that after that he requested the driver to stop the auto and to help the injured but he fled away from the spot along with auto.

PW2 stays that he was still inside the auto and after running about 1 km, driver of the offending vehicle deboarded him from his auto and immediately PW2 noted down the number of said auto bearing registration no.DL-1RU-5911.

PW2 further says that since he was scared he went to his house MACT No.27/2018 Page 5 and after 5-6 days he visited PS Jyoti Nagar and disclosed the facts of accident as well as registration number of auto being DL- 1RU-5911 to the police and police recorded his statement.
12. Nothing substantive came in the cross examination of PW2 to dent his testimony.

Although he stated that he does not know if injured was conscious or not after the accident as driver of the auto Dar - Satender vs Rais on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70538189/
3 fled away as soon as injured fell down.

13. Having considered the evidence of PW1 and PW2, this Tribunal finds that their evidence is cogent and specific with regard to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 in driving of offending vehicle no.DL-1RU-5911.
Moreover documents of criminal case annexed with DAR Ex.PW1/5 show that FIR No.443/2017 was registered in which respondent no.1 was charge sheeted.
The DAR also indicate that it is respondent no.1 who was responsible in causing of accident.
Moreover site plan, mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle no. DL-1RU- 5911.

Thus,
testimony of PW1 and PW2 coupled with material available on record clearly establish that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
Therefore this Tribunal concludes that petitioner has proved that accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent in in driving of offending vehicle no.DL-1RU-5911.
Accordingly issue stands decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
Issue No.2 14.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
MACT No.27/2018 Page 6 "Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future;
(ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort, disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
15. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the Dar - Satender vs Rais on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70538189/
4 accident.

The object of awarding MACT No.27/2018 Page 7 damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair,
reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general  damages)
 (iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
 (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of  prospects of marriage)
 (vi) Loss of expectation of life  (shortening of normal longevity).
MACT No.27/2018 Page 8

In routine personal injury cases,
compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the Dar - Satender vs Rais on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70538189/
5 evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
16.

sentences.text:
In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses:
17.
PW1 in his evidence states that he received major multiple injuries on his left leg in the form of amputation and also multiple abrasion on other parts of body due to which he became disabled.
He also stated that as his leg has a massive problem so his working capacity has been badly affected and he cannot walk and stand on his own without help of others.
He also stated that he received medical treatment in GTB Hospital and some other private hospitals also.
PW1 says that his treatment is still going on and he incurred expenses on his treatment including physiotherapy, conveyance and special diet to the tune of Rs.2,00,000/-.
He also says that he incurred medical expenses for a sum of Rs.50,000/- since the accident took place and Rs.1,00,000/- for purchasing prosthetic limb.

Petitioner has proved on record original discharge paper of GTB Hospital as Ex.PW1/3.
MACT No.27/2018 Page 9 18.
Perusal of documents Ex.PW1/3 shows that petitioner/ injured remained admitted in GTB Hospital from 31.10.2017 to 03.11.2017.

However no documentary evidence has been placed on record by the petitioner with regard to expenses incurred by him towards medical treatment in any other private hospital or bills/invoices of medicines.
So far as contention regarding purchase of prosthetic is concerned, no bill in this regard has been proved on record.
However it has come in the evidence of PW1 that his left leg above knee was amputated due to accidental injuries and prosthetic limb has been implanted.

As such this Tribunal is of the view that petitioner must have incurred some expenditure towards his medical treatment for the period of his treatment, on medicine bills,
prosthetic limb etc.
Therefore a compensation for a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

Loss of earning during treatment:
19.
Petitioner (PW1) in his evidence testified that because of the accidental injuries he received multiple grievous injuries on all over his body including amputation of his left leg above knee.
He stated that he is 8 th pass, unmarried and was working as a labourer with a mason in Delhi.
PW1 also says that nature of his work was totally dependent upon his legs and he used to earn Rs.15,000/- per month approximately.
He also says that it is very much difficulty for him to continue his work because of accident and he is unemployed since accident in question.

Dar - Satender vs Rais on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70538189/
6 20.

sentences.text: Claimant has claimed loss of income due to accidental injuries from the date of accident, however during cross- examination PW1 stated that he has not filed any income proof document and he does not have any document to prove further MACT No.27/2018 Page 10 expenses and prescription for his future treatment.
21. Ld. counsel for petitioner submits that income of the petitioner/injured should be assessed on the basis of minimum wags prevalent in Delhi as accident has taken place in Delhi.
Moreover the petitioner has been working as labourer in Delhi.

22. On the other hand ld. counsel for insurance company submits that Tribunal should fix the income of petitioner on the basis of minimum wages prevalent in UP because as per Aadhar card,
Identity card injured is resident of Budaun, Uttar Pradesh.
And there is no evidence showing that injured was working for gain in Delhi.

23. Having considered the submissions, question of ascertaining the income on the basis of minimum wages should be on the basis of fact that where the injured has been residing beside the evidence regarding the place of accident.
In the present case though accident has taken place in Delhi but there is no evidence showing that injured was residing in Delhi or working for gain in Delhi.

In such circumstance this Tribunal is of the considered view that income of the injured is to be assessed on the basis of minimum wages of unskilled worker prevalent in State of Uttar Pradesh at the time of accident which is Rs.7,400.48 per month.

24. Though petitioner has placed on record medical treatment record and bills/ invoices of pharmacy, however no document has been placed on record showing his admission in any of the hospitals except his admission GTB hospital from 31.10.2017 to 03.11.2017.
But fact remains that petitioner suffered multiple injuries on his whole body apart from amputation of his left leg above knee.

So taking into MACT No.27/2018 Page 11 consideration the injuries suffered by the petitioner and medical documents on record, this Tribunal is of considered view that petitioner is entitled for loss of earning for period of two months.
As such petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.14,800.96 (rounded of to Rs.14,801/-) (Rs.7,400.48 X 2 months) under this head.

Loss of future earning due to disability :
25.

In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:-
"9.
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.

This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
Dar - Satender vs Rais on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70538189/
7  (i) Whether the disablement is  permanent or temporary;
 (ii) If the disablement is permanent,
whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement;
(iii) If the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.

entities.text: Dar - Satender vs Rais on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will MACT No.27/2018 Page 12 proceed to ascertain its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."
....If doctor has given evidence about percentage of permanent disability, Tribunal will have to seek doctors opinion as to whether it is possible to deduce the corresponding functional permanent disability with reference to whole body and if so to what percentage.
13.
We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
(i). All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.
MACT No.27/2018 Page 13
(ii). The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as percentage of permanent disability).
Dar - Satender vs Rais on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70538189/
8 (iii).
The doctor who treated an injured- claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv). The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession, occupation or job, age, education and other factors."
26.

Keeping in view the ratio as discussed above, in the present case it is evident on record that as a result of the injuries sustained by petitioner in an accident, he suffered 80% permanent disability in relation to left lower limb.

In this regard PW3 Dr. Deepankar Verma, Sr. Resident, Orthopedic Department, GTB Hospital, Delhi, produced the record relating to disability certificate no.115/115/01/18 dated 29.01.2018, issued to injured Satendra Kumar which is Ex.PW1/4.
PW3 also stated that disability in this case is permanent in nature.

27. The disablement and loss of earning capacity are MACT No.27/2018 Page 14 two different aspects and may not corresponding to each other and the loss of income has to be seen considering the profession in which the petitioner was engaged at the time of accident.

As per case of petitioner,
he was working as labourer with a mason.

It came in the evidence of petitioner that due to accidental injury his left leg above knee has been amputated and prosthetic limb has been implanted due to which is working capacity has been badly affected.
Petitioner has categorically stated that he cannot walk and stand on his own without help of others and he was restricted to bed number of months since the day of accident.
28. In Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (supra) Hon'ble Apex Court in para 11 and 12 has observed that Tribunal should not be a silent spectator when medical evidence is tendered regarding injuries.

Tribunal is required to hold inquiry into the claim for determining just compensation by assessing the medical permanent disability as well as functional disability keeping in view nature of work,
profession etc. of the injured.
The percentage of permanent disability of whole body cannot be presumed to be percentage loss of earning.
Therefore Tribunal is bound to assess corresponding functional disability to compute the future loss of income.

29. Having considered the entire evidence, medical documents reflect that petitioner suffered grievous injuries in the accident in question including amputation of his left leg above knee for which prosthetic limb has been implanted.
His permanent disability to the extent of 80% is also in relation to left lower limb.

In such circumstances when petitioner was admittedly working as daily wager labourer, he must be having difficulty in doing day to day work and his working capacity has MACT No.27/2018 Page 15 completely halted due to accidental injuries.

As such this Tribunal finds that the functional disability to whole body of the petitioner may be considered to be 100% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of his future income because keeping in view the nature of work although medical disability of the injured may be upto 80% but this Tribunal assess that his injury must have affected his functional capacity upto 100%.

Dar - Satender vs Rais on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70538189/
9 30.

Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer:
Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].

entities.text: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per photocopy of Aadhar card Ex.PW1/1 and PAN card, date of birth of petitioner is 01.01.1991.
As such age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e. 31.10.2017 was around 26 years.

As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 17 as applicable to age group between 26-30 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.

Moreover, the law has been well settled by the decisions of Supreme Court in the cases of Sandeep Khanuja (supra) and Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., 2020 SCC OnLine SC 601, that while applying the multiplier method, future prospects on advancement in life and career are also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., 2020 SCC OnLine SC 601
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, considering the petitioner being below 40 years at the time of accident, an addition of income to the extent of 40% towards future prospects has to be counted.

31. As discussed above, the income of petitioner has been assessed as Rs. Rs.7,400.48 + 40%
(Rs.2,960.19), total Rs.10,360.67 (Rs.7,400.48 + Rs.2,960.19).
Thus applying the functional disability to be 100% of Rs.10,360.67, amount comes MACT No.27/2018 Page 16 out to be Rs.10,360.67.
As such the loss of future income due to disability comes out to be Rs.10,360.67 X 12 X 17 = Rs.21,13,577/-.
Special Diet & Conveyance Charges:
32. Petitioner/injured (PW1) in his evidence has deposed that he has incurred expenses of Rs.30,000/- for conveyance.
This Tribunal has already awarded compensation towards medical expenses to the petitioner while assessing his period of treatment of two months.

It has also come in the evidence that due to accidental injuries, petitioner suffered grievous injuries on his body including amputation of his left leg above knee for which he has to take prosthetic limb.
It has also come in the evidence of PW1 that after discharge from hospital he is continuing facing difficulty in day to day life and still taking treatment.

In view of evidence of PW1/petitioner, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioner must have incurred expenses on his special diet and spent money on conveyance charges for going to hospital for follow up treatment.
Therefore this Tribunal assesses special diet to the tune of Rs.20,000/- and conveyance charges of Rs.20,000/-.
Thus, it would be in the interest of justice to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards special diet and a sum of Rs.20,000/- as conveyance charges to the petitioner.

Attendant Charges:
33.

As it has already come in the evidence that petitioner remained admitted in hospital, operation was conducted on his left leg and prosthetic limb was placed in his left leg as well as the fact that petitioner remained under follow up treatment for a considerable period of time.

Thus, keeping in view medical difficulties faced by the petitioner, this Tribunal awards MACT No.27/2018 Page 17 compensation towards attendant charges payable to unskilled labour i.e. Rs.7,400.48 X 2 months which comes out to be Rs.14,800.96/- (rounded of to Rs.14,801/-).
NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES :

Dar - Satender vs Rais on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70538189/
10

Pain & Sufferings:
34.

While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No: 709/02, date of decision:
02.02.2007 can be considered:
"12. On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.
However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objectives co-relation with the pain and suffering.

13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:
(a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."
35.
In this case, as per medical documents of petitioner, he was found to have suffered grievous injuries all over his body.
His treatment record annexed with DAR as well as disability certificate Ex.PW1/4 show that left leg of petitioner above knee had to be amputated and he has been taking continuous treatment.

Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.25,000/-
would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
Accordingly, Rs.25,000/- is granted to the MACT No.27/2018 Page 18 petitioner under this head.

Loss of Amenities:
36.

It is evident on record that even after completion of treatment, petitioner sustained 80%
permanent physical disability in relation to left lower limb which has been assessed as 100%
functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner by this Tribunal keeping in view the nature of work he was involved being a labourer.
It cannot be ignored that with the aforementioned disability, petitioner is bound to face difficulties throughout his life and will not be able to enjoy the amenities of life to the fullest.
In view of this, the petitioner is granted a compensation of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.

Respondent no.3/insurance has not disputed the fact that offending vehicle/TSR No.DL 1RU 5999 was insured with it under the policy no.0157555699 in the name of Sunil Kumar under the category auto security commercial package policy.

Respondent no.3 has taken two fold pleas regarding the liability, firstly that petitioner/injured was sitting by the side of driver seat in the TSR whereas as per the registration certificate as well as insurance policy, sitting capacity of said TSR was 3+1 which means that three passengers plus driver.
As per the insurance company in the present case injured was additionally sitting in the TSR beside three passengers and driver

,
consequently there was a breach of insurance policy.

Secondly it is further the plea that TSR permit was issued in the name of registered owner of the TSR namely Sunil Kumar and as per the permit,
only owner of the TSR can drive the vehicle and no one else.
It is stated that even under the insurance policy this was one of the condition and same stated to have been violated.
41. Insurance company has examined two witnesses in order to prove above said two pleas.
R3W1 is Devender Kumar from Auto Rickshaw unit of Transport Department Burari who proved the permit of offending vehicle no. DL 1RU 5999 Ex.R3W1/1.
This witness states that as per the record owner of the vehicle can only drive that vehicle and no one else, for which permit has been issued.

PW R3W2 is Ms.P. Keerthy, Sr. Manager of respondent no.3 company who also deposed that petitioner was additionally sitting in the TSR in question beside MACT No.27/2018 Page 20 three passengers and driver.

This witness further deposed that at the time of accident TSR was being driven by respondent no.1 herein whereas the permit for the said TSR was in the name of registered owner i.e.
Sunil Kumar.
PW R3W2 further says that as per the terms of the policy also only registered owner/permit holder can drive the TSR.

This witness proved insurance policy Ex.R3W2/1 as well as notification of Delhi Government dated 08.08.2012 Ex.R3W2/2.

12 42.

Counsel for the petitioner submits that there is no legal requirement that only permit holder can drive the TSR and that in case anyone else who is otherwise having valid DL, was driving the TSR,
there would not be any liability for insurance.

43. Having considered the submissions and evidence, of R3W1 and R3W2, it is established proposition that if a transport vehicle has been insured subject to certain terms and conditions including the condition regarding keeping a valid permit.
Obviously the owner of the TSR has to comply those terms and conditions of insurance policy.
From the permit Ex.R3W1/1 it is very much explicit that under the permit only the person in whose favour said permit in respect of TSR No. DL 1RU 5999 had been issued, can drive the same.
In the present case admittedly at the time of accident permit holder of said TSR was not driving it.
This in itself amounts to breach of condition not only of permit but also terms of insurance policy.
This Tribunal need not to go into the question of another plea that the injured was the additional passenger than the maximum capacity of the TSR as there is no sufficient evidence in this regard.

From going through the evidence of witnesses noted above as well as documents proved including permit conditions and insurance MACT No.27/2018 Page 21 policy, this Tribunal is of the considered view that on account of breach of policy terms, though respondent no.3 is liable to pay the compensation amount but is given recovery rights of the amount of compensation from the registered owner of TSR No. DL 1RU 5999 namely Sunil Kumar (respondent no.2).

(2)Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.
After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."
....If doctor has given evidence about percentage of permanent disability, Tribunal will have to seek doctors opinion as to whether it is possible to deduce the corresponding functional permanent disability with reference to whole body and if so to what percentage.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others.
(MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.
Thus,
testimony of PW1 and PW2 coupled with material available on record clearly establish that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.
The object of awarding MACT No.27/2018 Page 7 damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair,
reasonable and equitable manner.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.
(i). All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.
(ii). The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.
The doctor who treated an injured- claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.
Tribunal is required to hold inquiry into the claim for determining just compensation by assessing the medical permanent disability as well as functional disability keeping in view nature of work,
profession etc. of the injured.
The percentage of permanent disability of whole body cannot be presumed to be percentage loss of earning.
Therefore Tribunal is bound to assess corresponding functional disability to compute the future loss of income.
29. Having considered the entire evidence, medical documents reflect that petitioner suffered grievous injuries in the accident in question including amputation of his left leg above knee for which prosthetic limb has been implanted.
His permanent disability to the extent of 80% is also in relation to left lower limb.
In such circumstances when petitioner was admittedly working as daily wager labourer, he must be having difficulty in doing day to day work and his working capacity has MACT No.27/2018 Page 15 completely halted due to accidental injuries.
As such this Tribunal finds that the functional disability to whole body of the petitioner may be considered to be 100% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of his future income because keeping in view the nature of work although medical disability of the injured may be upto 80% but this Tribunal assess that his injury must have affected his functional capacity upto 100%.

Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer:
Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].
As such age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e. 31.10.2017 was around 26 years.
Moreover, the law has been well settled by the decisions of Supreme Court in the cases of Sandeep Khanuja (supra) and Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., 2020 SCC OnLine SC 601, that while applying the multiplier method, future prospects on advancement in life and career are also to be taken into consideration.
In this case, as per medical documents of petitioner, he was found to have suffered grievous injuries all over his body.
Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.25,000/-
would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.

And there is no evidence showing that injured was working for gain in Delhi.
23. Having considered the submissions, question of ascertaining the income on the basis of minimum wages should be on the basis of fact that where the injured has been residing beside the evidence regarding the place of accident.
In the present case though accident has taken place in Delhi but there is no evidence showing that injured was residing in Delhi or working for gain in Delhi.
In such circumstance this Tribunal is of the considered view that income of the injured is to be assessed on the basis of minimum wages of unskilled worker prevalent in State of Uttar Pradesh at the time of accident which is Rs.7,400.48 per month.
As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 17 as applicable to age group between 26-30 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.
